chunks: And by this chain, He (peace be upon him) said:
The first one to be grey-haired was Ibrahim (peace be upon him). He said: 'O Lord, what is this?' So He said: 'A radiance and a reverence.' He said: 'Lord, increase for me from it.'

key_terms.إِبْرَاهِيمُ: Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham), peace be upon him
key_terms.تَوْقِيرٌ: Reverence or respect, indicating dignity and status
key_terms.شَابَ: To become grey-haired (specifically referring to the hair of the head)
key_terms.نُورٌ: Light or radiance, indicating spiritual illumination

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of grey hair in Islam according to the hadith of Prophet Ibrahim?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this narration from al-Kafi highlights the spiritual dignity of aging, interpreting grey hair not as decay but as a divine sign of 'radiance' (nur) and 'reverence' (tawqir). This perspective encourages believers to view the physical signs of aging as opportunities for increased spiritual stature and divine favor, rather than mere biological decline.

en.hubeali: ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The first one to be grey-haired was Ibrahim<sup>as</sup>. He<sup>as</sup> said: ‘O Lord<sup>azwj</sup>! What is this?’ So He<sup>azwj</sup> Said: “A radiance and a reverence”. He<sup>as</sup> said: ‘Lord<sup>azwj</sup>! Increase for me<sup>as</sup>, from it’.
en.sarwar: 4. Through the same chain of narrators as that of the previous Hadith the following is narrated: “He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
The first one who noticed gray hairs was Ibrahim ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and he asked, ‘O Lord, what is this?’ He said, ‘It is light and reverence.’ He then said, ‘O Lord, increase it for me.’”
